Hi Rafael,

We're working through the SIG/SOC2 questionnaires and the reviewer has flagged activity logs and admin/audit trails. Could you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted API (production) environment: 

- What event categories are logged for admin/operator activity (examples: API key changes, model rollouts, role grants, console logins, snapshot exports)?
- Default retention window and any options for extending/shortening it per account (and how that differs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments).
- Can we request a point-in-time export / signed snapshot for a specified UTC window? What formats, checksums, and custody metadata do you provide?
- Is there a streaming/export integration (S3 or SIEM) we can enable for continuous ingest?
- Redaction options: can we request PII redaction or field-level redaction prior to export?

We're aiming to include a short description + an evidence artifact in our SIG response. If you can provide a template manifest/schema and an estimated turnaround time for a one-off 30-day snapshot, that would be ideal.

I've attached the SIG_questionnaire_v2.pdf with the specific question references.

Can we target a short call if needed — cc'd our legal ops for evidence handling preferences.

Thanks,
Ben Turner
Security & Compliance, MedicoSys

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Retention & access window for activity ledger - SOC2/SIG request

Ben —

Thanks for the clear list. TL;DR answers up front, details and artifacts below. Happy to hop on a 30-min sync if you want to walk through specifics.

What we log (high level)
- Admin console auth events (successful/failed) and IP/region.
- Role & policy changes (create/update/delete).
- API key lifecycle events (create/rotate/revoke).
- Model serving changes: model version pin, rollout/canary start/stop.
- Infrastructure/operator actions: node drains, maintenance, escalations.
- Export/manifest actions (who requested, timestamps, delivery URL).

Retention windows
- Hosted (default): 13 months by default; can be extended to 25 months via an add-on for customers on enterprise plans.
- Dedicated: configurable retention per pool; typical defaults 13/25/36 months depending on contract.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): retention determined by customer configuration; our agent supports TTL policies and local snapshots.

Exports & snapshots
- We support on-demand point-in-time snapshots for any UTC window (start/end). Format options: gzipped newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or CSV export of the ledger. Each export includes a manifest (JSON) with SHA256 checksums for each file, record counts, start/end timestamps, and an audit chain (requester, job id, operator).
- Delivery: presigned S3 link (configurable expiry), Transfer appliance for very large bundles (enterprise), or direct SFTP (per agreement).
- We can also provide an append-only signed manifest (internal signature) to prove integrity.

Streaming integrations
- Continuous streaming to customer-owned S3 (parquet / gzipped NDJSON), or to common SIEM endpoints via HTTP-forwarder (TLS + mTLS).

Redaction options
- We support field-level redaction rules in the export pipeline. PII can be hashed or removed; you can provide a schema for fields to redact. Redaction is applied as a build step before packaging; full raw logs can be retained internally for 90 days (forensic retention) depending on contract.

Turnaround & artifacts
- One-off 30-day snapshot (standard request) — typical turnaround 3 business days for Hosted if no redaction required; 5–7 business days if custom redaction or manifest signing is requested.
- Attached: activity_ledger_schema_v1.csv (column list + types) and a sample manifest template.

Next steps
1) Confirm which environment and the UTC window you want for the canary export (we recommend a 24-hour window first).
2) Tell us desired export format (NDJSON or CSV) and whether you need field redaction.
3) We'll create a small scoped job and share a presigned link for download.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Retention & access window for activity ledger - SOC2/SIG request

Ben / Rafael —

Adding the technical details you asked for so MedicoSys can map fields to the SIG matrix. Short version + a sample path.

Format & fields
- Canonical export: NDJSON (one JSON object per line). Core envelope fields: ts (RFC3339), event_id (uuid4), service, actor_id, actor_role, action, target, ip, region, request_id, correlation_ids (list), prev_state_digest (hex), metadata (map).
- Checksums: each exported chunk includes a per-file SHA256 and the manifest contains an overall Merkle-root like digest (we use a concatenated SHA256 over sorted file checksums).
- Sequence & ordering: exports are sequence-numbered; each event contains a monotonic seq_no to detect gaps.

Storage & custody
- Internal staging S3 path for evidence jobs (read-only for customers via presigned URLs): s3://redwood-evidence/medicosys/2027-09-14/
- We record operator request audit entries (who created the export job, when, and whether redaction was applied).

Redaction pipeline
- Redaction is deterministic: hash(field) or redact-to-NULL; we record a redaction_manifest with policy id and fields redacted. Redaction is applied during packaging and cannot be reversed on the delivered bundle (raw internal copies retained per contract).

Automation & APIs
- Exports can be requested via Console or the Evidence API (POST /v1/evidence/jobs with window and redaction parameters). Job status is traceable via the API and the console; completed jobs produce a manifest and presigned links.

Attachment: export_playbook.md (contains sample API calls, manifest example, and verification commands).

If you want a canary job, send the UTC start/end for a 24-hour window and whether you want NDJSON vs CSV and redaction enabled.

—Karthik
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
attachments: export_playbook.md
